references.text: The psalmist describes that the heavens and earth will perish, but God remains the same. This underscores the transience of creation in contrast to God's eternal word, as Jesus says in [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33].

Isaiah proclaims that "the grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever." This is a fundamental Old Testament parallel to Jesus' statement that his words will never pass away ([ref:Jes 40:8|Isaiah 40:8]).

Isaiah says that the heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth will grow old like a garment, but God's salvation will last forever. This points to the same theme as in [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33]: creation passes away, but God's word endures.
Jesus says in the Sermon on the Mount that not the smallest letter or stroke of the law will pass away. This confirms the eternal validity of God's word, in line with [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33].

The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says exactly the same thing: "Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away." This is the closest parallel to [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33].

The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus declares the same: "Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away." Together with [ref:Matt 24:35|Matthew 24:35], these form the synoptic parallels to [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33].

The book of Hebrews quotes [ref:Sal 102:26-27|Psalm 102:26–27] about how the heavens and earth will perish like a garment, but the Lord remains. This supports Jesus' words that his own words are more enduring than all creation.

Peter describes the day of the Lord when the heavens will pass away with a roar and the elements will be dissolved in fire. This confirms Jesus' statement in [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33] that heaven and earth will pass away.

John sees a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away. This is the final fulfillment of what Jesus predicted in [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33] about heaven and earth passing away.

Peter quotes [ref:Jes 40:8|Isaiah 40:8] that all flesh is like grass that withers, but the Lord's word remains forever. This confirms the eternal nature of God's word as Jesus emphasizes in [ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33].
